messages.subject: SAM fit indices interpretation
parts:
I ran local SAM and for the structural part, the fit indices are found to be:
chisq df cfi rmsea srmr 0 0 1 0 0
Does not this indicate a perfect fit? This seems suspicious, too good to be true. 
Can anyone help me with the interpretation? In the paper (Rossee & Loh, 2024), I see no discussion about it.
Also, is there a reason/a possibility to ignore the fit indices in SAM and focus on the  coefficients (e.g., of the regression or paths)?

Thanks

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: SAM fit indices interpretation
parts:
On 2/5/25 4:49 AM, Gairan Pamei wrote:
> I ran local SAM and for the structural part, the fit indices are found
> to be:
> chisq df cfi rmsea srmr 0 0 1 0 0
> Does not this indicate a perfect fit? This seems suspicious, too good to
> be true.

This is perfectly normal. It simply indicates that the structural part
of your model is saturated. This is not a bad thing per se. It just
means there is no way to 'test' the structural model. But you can still
interpret the coefficients. (BTW: all regression models are saturated).

> Also, is there a reason/a possibility to ignore the fit indices in SAM
> and focus on the  coefficients (e.g., of the regression or paths)?

Only when the (structural) part is saturated. Otherwise, you should
report the fit indices.

In addition, I would also report the chi-square values (and degrees of
freedom) of the measurement blocks.

Yves.
